result.question:
Adversarially verify whether a specific research gap is truly empty as of September 2026. The claimed gap: "there is NO prior published work combining ALL of — (1) bi-temporal DEEP-LEARNING semantic change detection / segmentation for burned-area mapping, (2) South Korean SPRING wildfires specifically, (3) explicitly handling the spring green-up / phenology confound that reverses or suppresses the optical dNBR burn signal, and (4) generalization to UNSEEN fires (cross-fire / out-of-domain), using free optical satellite (Sentinel-2 / Landsat)."

GOAL: try HARD to DISPROVE the gap by finding any paper/preprint/thesis that fills it or comes close. Search exhaustively, including Korean-language venues.

Cover these angles:
1. Korean wildfire burned-area / burn-severity mapping with deep learning (any: U-Net, CNN, transformer, change detection) — list ALL you can find 2019-2026, with authors/venue/year, sensor, method, and whether they address spring/phenology or unseen-fire generalization. Include Korean fires: Uljin/Samcheok 2022, Andong, Uiseong/Sancheong/Yeongdeok 2025, Gangneung, Goseong 2019, NIFoS/산림청/원명수/차성은 works.
2. Any study explicitly addressing the SPRING green-up / phenology / leaf-out confound in dNBR / burned-area detection (Korea OR elsewhere — East Asia, temperate deciduous/mixed forests) and how they mitigate it (phenology-detrended indices like ASAP/pdSI, seasonal matching, tight bracketing, SWIR/char indices).
3. Bi-temporal DEEP-LEARNING change detection applied to wildfire burn scars (not building/land-cover) with cross-region or unseen-fire generalization evaluation — global, and whether any use Korean data.
4. Korean-language / KCI / domestic remote sensing journal papers (대한원격탐사학회지, 한국지리정보학회, GIS) on 산불 피해지 변화탐지 / 딥러닝 산불 탐지 — 2019-2026.
5. Datasets/benchmarks for burned-area segmentation that include Korea or temperate spring fires (CaBuAr, CBAS, MTBS, any Korean burn dataset).

For each found work, state precisely which of the 4 gap-conditions it satisfies and which it MISSES, so we can judge if the 4-way intersection is genuinely empty or already occupied. Distinguish full-text-verified from abstract/snippet-only, and Korean-language sources explicitly. Conclude: is the 4-way gap truly empty, partially filled, or occupied? If partially filled, name the closest prior work and exactly what it lacks.
result.summary: The 4-way research gap is GENUINELY EMPTY as of September 2026: no single published work combines (1) bi-temporal deep-learning semantic change detection for burned area, (2) South Korean SPRING wildfires, (3) explicit handling of the spring green-up/phenology confound that reverses/suppresses the optical dNBR signal, AND (4) generalization to unseen (cross-fire/out-of-domain) fires, using free optical satellite. Across all 12 verified works, each condition is occupied by SOME paper, but the maximum any single paper reaches is THREE of the four conditions. The single closest prior work is Cha & Won et al. (2022, Korean Journal of Remote Sensing), which uniquely satisfies (1)+(2)+(4) — a U-Net bi-temporal CNN trained on the Gangneung-Donghae spring 2022 fire and applied cross-fire to Uljin-Samcheok — but it never addresses the spring green-up/phenology confound (condition 3), the exact axis the gap hinges on. Conversely, the only work that squarely documents and quantifies the Korean spring green-up/dNBR-reversal confound (Youn & Jeong 2019) is a single-event dNBR index study with no deep learning and no cross-fire test, so it misses (1) and (4). No paper — Korean-language KCI/KJRS, MDPI, or international (BiAU-Net, FLOGA) — closes the intersection; the gap is unoccupied.

findings.claim: The 4-way intersection is genuinely EMPTY: no single work satisfies all of (1) bi-temporal DL semantic change detection + (2) South Korean spring fires + (3) explicit spring green-up/phenology-confound handling + (4) unseen-fire generalization on free optical satellite.
findings.vote: synthesis of 22 confirmed claims (all 3-0 except two 2-1)
findings.evidence: Every verified work occupies at most 3 of the 4 conditions. The two papers that jointly touch the most distinctive axes are disjoint: Cha & Won 2022 covers (1)+(2)+(4) but not (3); Youn & Jeong 2019 covers (3) but not (1) or (4). No paper, Korean or international, was found combining all four. The full-text-verified international bi-temporal DL works (BiAU-Net, FLOGA) are non-Korean and non-spring and do not address the phenology confound. The gap is therefore genuinely empty/unoccupied.

findings.claim: Cha & Won et al. (2022) is the CLOSEST prior work: a U-Net bi-temporal CNN applied to Korean spring 2022 fires with cross-fire (unseen-fire) evaluation — satisfying conditions (1), (2), (4) — but it MISSES condition (3), never discussing or mitigating the spring green-up/phenology confound.
findings.evidence: Korean-language KCI paper (대한원격탐사학회지 Vol.38 No.6.1, 2022). Uses U-net-based CNNs with bi-temporal spectral-band differencing (Feb-Mar, Feb-Apr) on Gangneung-Donghae spring fire (2022.03.05-08), then applies the same model cross-fire to Uljin-Samcheok (2022.03.04-13) reaching 74.4% overlap with NIFoS reference (reported F1 0.470/IoU 0.899 on the unseen fire; note the F1/IoU pairing is internally inconsistent in the paper itself). Uses NDVI/NDWI temporal differences, not dNBR, and does NOT explicitly discuss or mitigate the phenology confound — condition (3) genuinely missed. This is the single work lacking only condition (3), the axis the gap hinges on.

findings.claim: The only work that explicitly documents and quantifies the Korean spring green-up/phenology confound reversing/suppressing the dNBR signal (Youn & Jeong 2019) satisfies condition (3) but is a single-event dNBR index study with NO deep learning and NO cross-fire test — missing conditions (1) and (4).
findings.evidence: Korean-language KJRS 35(6-2):1107-1115, 2019, on the April 2019 Sokcho/Goseong spring fire using 7 multi-temporal Sentinel-2A images. Quantifies that late-April/early-May green-up produces dNBR classifications contradicting NDVI ('식생이 급격하게 증가하는 4월 말에서 5월 초에서 NDVI의 결과값과 상반된 분류결과'), directly diagnosing the phenology confound. But method is index-based dNBR (7 severity classes), NOT deep learning, and it is a single-event case study with no cross-fire/out-of-domain validation. Occupies only condition (3); actively supports (does not fill) the gap.

findings.claim: International bi-temporal deep-learning burned-area change-detection works (BiAU-Net 2024, FLOGA/BAM-CD 2023-24) satisfy conditions (1) and (4) with strong cross-region generalization, but are non-Korean, non-spring, and do NOT address the spring green-up/phenology confound — missing (2) and (3).
findings.evidence: BiAU-Net (Int. J. Applied Earth Obs. Geoinf., 2024, full-text verified via Glasgow eprints) is a bi-temporal pre/post Sentinel-2 U-Net+attention model trained on one fire (Chico, California) and tested on five cross-continental areas (Australia, Spain, Indonesia, Kenya) — strong condition (4) — but 'spring/phenology/green-up' appear only in its reference list, and no study region is Korea. FLOGA (arXiv 2311.03339 / IEEE JSTARS 2024) is a bi-temporal Sentinel-2+MODIS change-detection dataset with the BAM-CD model, but covers only Greece 2017-2021 (Mediterranean, 55% of fires in July-August) and mentions phenology only as a passing spectral-index sensitivity. Both satisfy (1)+(4), miss (2)+(3).

findings.claim: Korean single-temporal / spectral-index / non-bitemporal works cluster near the gap but each misses the bi-temporal-DL condition (1) and/or others: Son/Lee et al. 2024 (single-temporal, 14 KR fires, 2-region hold-out), Chae & Choi 2024 (single post-fire U-Net), Lee/Yang et al. 2022 (bi-temporal-input ML but no cross-fire test), and the Uljin index study 2022.
findings.evidence: Son/Lee et al. 2024 (Remote Sensing 16:884) is SINGLE-temporal DL (U-Net/HRNet, IoU 89.40/82.49 on two held-out KR fires) — partial condition-4 signal but explicitly avoids bi-temporal differencing (misses 1). Chae & Choi 2024 (대한지리학회지, DBpia NODE11763999) is single post-fire U-Net semantic segmentation on 353 images/303 events (misses 1, bi-temporal). Lee/Yang et al. 2022 (Applied Sciences 12:10077) uses bi-temporal pre+post+difference inputs with U-Net/LightGBM/RF on two KR sites (Andong+Uljin) but uses within-scene 60/40 split, no cross-fire hold-out (misses 4). The Uljin 2022 index study (KJRS) and FBI index (KCI ART002308810, 2017) are spectral-index, not DL (miss 1). None combines all four conditions.

findings.claim: Adjacent Korean U-Net change-detection work exists but is NOT wildfire: Pyo/Han et al. 2022 applies U-Net to general forest change detection (landslide/deforestation motivation) via post-classification comparison of airborne imagery — irrelevant to burned-area condition (1).
findings.evidence: Forests 2022, 13:2170. U-Net segments single-date forest/non-forest, then post-classification-compares two years per province (Chungcheong 2009-2016, Gangwon 2010-2019, etc.) for landslide-prevention monitoring using AIRBORNE (not Sentinel-2) imagery. No wildfire, burn severity, dNBR, or spring/phenology content. Tests cross-region generalization (touches condition 4) but misses the burned-area sense of condition (1) entirely. Confirms it is a separate, non-competing line of work.

result.caveats: Two 2-1 split votes underlie secondary details: claim [4] (Son/Lee 2024 two-region hold-out as a partial generalization signal) and claim [8]/[6] scoping — these do not change the top-line verdict since neither paper claims condition (3). Several primary sources returned HTTP 403/404 on direct fetch (ScienceDirect, MDPI, ResearchGate, the original Uljin URL); their load-bearing facts were verified via independent mirrors (Glasgow eprints open-access PDF for BiAU-Net, kjrs.org for the Uljin study, koreascience.kr and KCI for the Korean papers, arXiv HTML for FLOGA) and cross-confirmed search snippets, so verification is strong but for a few papers rests on abstract-level rather than full-text reading (notably Pyo/Han 2022 phenology-absence is inferred from abstract, which is safe because the paper is not about wildfire). The Cha & Won 2022 reported metrics (F1 0.470 vs IoU 0.899) are mathematically inconsistent within the paper itself and should be cited with that caveat. Time-sensitivity: this is a September 2026 snapshot; the gap could be filled by any 2026 preprint not yet indexed, and Korean domestic conference proceedings (non-KCI) are harder to surface exhaustively. The refuted claims confirm that neither the Uljin index study nor the FBI index paper genuinely handles the phenology confound as a methodological solution — they at most note it descriptively.
openQuestions: Is there a 2025-2026 preprint or Korean conference paper (non-KCI proceedings, KOGSIS, 대한원격탐사학회 학술대회) applying bi-temporal DL change detection to the Uiseong/Sancheong/Yeongdeok 2025 spring fires that would newly occupy the gap?

Would adding explicit phenology-confound handling (ASAP/pdSI phenology-detrended index, SWIR/char index, or tight seasonal bracketing) to the Cha & Won 2022 bi-temporal U-Net architecture constitute the first work to close the 4-way intersection — i.e., is the gap fillable by a modest extension of the closest prior work?

Do any Korean burned-area datasets/benchmarks with cross-fire hold-out splits exist beyond the informal 14-fire/303-event collections used in single-temporal studies (NIFoS/산림청 vector labels), or is dataset scarcity the binding constraint on satisfying condition 4 for spring fires specifically?
Has BiAU-Net or FLOGA/BAM-CD been independently tested (drop-in transfer) on Korean spring fires, and if so did the spring green-up confound cause the documented dNBR-reversal failure mode?

refuted.claim: The study EXPLICITLY addresses the Korean spring green-up / phenology confound that suppresses the burn signal, mitigating it via seasonally synchronized before/after imagery (Feb-May), satisfying gap condition #3.

The paper explicitly targets the phenology/seasonal confound of dNBR by designing an index the authors claim works regardless of season, addressing gap-condition (3) the spring green-up / phenology confound.
